items.title: Scott Miller thinks Australia probably hates him. He's desperate to reverse the damage
items.description: From Olympic silver medallist to convicted drug supplier, Scott Miller opens up on one of the biggest downfalls in the history of Australian sport and the moments that saved his life as he seeks redemption.

items.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz but US says traffic is flowing
items.description: Iran says it has closed the Strait of Hormuz over Israel's continued attacks in Lebanon, which killed at least 16 people on Saturday, local time.

items.title: War helped 're-enliven' Iran's regime. Trump's truce may complicate that
items.description: For decades the Islamic republic has been using its "main enemy" America to distract from its repressive regime, analysts say. But the recent truce with Donald Trump could change that.

items.title: On health and child care, Labor might have found Pauline Hanson's kryptonite
items.description: Pauline Hanson said thousands of words in her marathon appearance at the National Press Club, but only a few of them will be heard widely.

items.title: More missiles and ditch the UN: What One Nation’s foreign policy looks like
items.description: With One Nation running red hot in the polls and posing a serious challenge to the incumbent parties, there's more scrutiny on what its foreign policy would mean for Australia.

items.title: Live: Germany finds last-gasp winner against Côte d'Ivoire, Netherlands thump Sweden
items.description: Deniz Undav comes off the bench to score twice as Germany claims a late win over Côte d'Ivoire after the Netherlands beat Sweden 5-1. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel price cuts extended through July, but discount drops by half
items.description: The federal government is winding back its discount to the fuel excise over the next month as the 32 cents per litre fuel discount will drop to 16 cents.

items.title: The quest for the truth behind Australian nurses' massacre in WWII
items.description: A relative of one of the 21 Australian nurses massacred by Japanese soldiers on a remote Indonesian beach in WWII wants the real story of what happened to be told.

items.title: Police speech stuns descendants gathered at site of outback mass killing
items.description: Ronnie's great-grandfather collected bones and teeth from an outback creek bed. Now police say they're 'not proud' of what occurred.

items.title: Pitched as an outback oasis, this remote town is 'actually reinventing itself'
items.description: A decade after the last coal truck rumbled out of Leigh Creek, Baljit Singh Bajwa put millions of dollars on the line to invest in the shrinking mining town.

items.title: Al Jazeera cameraman killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
items.description: Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes have killed at least 11 people, including two children and an Al Jazeera cameraman, in the latest violence to rock the Palestinian territory despite a ceasefire.

items.title: 'Yanks flying up in the air': The World War II brawl that consumed Brisbane
items.description: The American war effort made Brisbane its stronghold in 1942, and thousands of attractive American soldiers were situated in Brisbane. That didn't sit so well with the Australians.

items.title: Six years on, officers relive one of Victoria Police's darkest days
items.description: The deaths of four Victoria Police officers on April 22, 2020 sent shock waves through the force, with the impacts of Eastern Freeway tragedy still felt six years on.

items.title: The adoption centre helping lab rats find their forever homes
items.description: A first-of-its kind adoption centre is aiming to find permanent homes for small animals used in scientific research.

items.title: It's the winter solstice, but you can expect more cold, dark mornings
items.description: The June solstice is the shortest day of the year in Australia, but not the one with the latest sunrise or coldest weather. Here's why.

items.title: Is 'baby brain' real? A neuroscientist explains
items.description: The fog new parents feel is real, but it seems to be driven less by motherhood rewiring the brain than by exhaustion, overload and the relentless demands of caring for a tiny human.

items.title: Did you pay attention at school? Let's see about that
items.description: Think you can get 10 out of 10 on our spelling quiz? Just remember, autocorrect can't save you here.

items.title: 'Old wine in a new bottle': Activists raise alarm over deepfake videos
items.description: AI-generated deepfake videos of prominent West Papuan rights campaigners spark concerns about how disinformation is being used as a form of "digital colonisation".

items.title: How this bus stop that hasn't changed cost a city almost $9m
items.description: Repeated failed attempts to shift this bus stop has cost ratepayers millions over the past 15 years. The council is now trying again, but some warn it is already "a dog's breakfast".

items.title: Ticketless travel for Melbourne trams has arrived
items.description: From today, Melbourne tram commuters can use their credit card, phone or smartwatch to get around.

items.title: Why a trip to Asia might be a good idea now
items.description: The war in the Middle East has not stopped Australians travelling but their preferences may be changing.

items.title: Bird flu could be catastrophic for nation's vulnerable species, experts warn
items.description: The black swan, the Tasmanian devil and Australian sea lions are among the species at risk if a deadly strain of avian influenza takes hold in Australia, experts are warning.

items.title: Police investigate fatal shooting in Melbourne's north-west
items.description: A crime scene is established in Ascot Vale after a man in his 30s was fatally shot.

items.title: Racism, bias led to 'superficial investigation' of teen's death
items.description: NSW Coroner's Court has found racial attitudes played a central role in the police investigation into Mark Haines's death 38 years ago.

items.title: 'It's about all the girls in Afghanistan': Cricketers play for recognition
items.description: In a bid for recognition, the Afghanistan women's cricket team will travel to England for the T20 World Cup — an event they cannot play in.
